result.cost:
Measured on the local SwiftShader renderer as CPU seconds of Chromium's GPU process per saved still, read from /proc. This does not depend on machine load; wall time under load 20 ranked a before/after pair the wrong way round. Before -> after:
- Halapē, ch1 1787 (steady frame): 63.7 -> 63.9 s. An earlier version of the gate reached 121.8 s until the water fade and the 3 % octave skip were added.
- ch1 1526 (first frame of the page): 180.1 -> 241.1 s (+34 %).
- Pali, ch2 3067 (first frame) and 3148 (steady): 112.2 / 107.5 -> 166.6 / 162.2 s (+50 %). The slope that was a smooth band is now textured, which costs more.
- ch3 7398 (sand with motion trails, first frame): 350.8 -> 561.2 s (+60 %) for little visible gain. A cheaper soil pass is a possible later step.
- Bigisland wide, ch2 4958: identical picture, detail is off there.
Final renders run on the Colab L4, where this cost has not been measured.

result.notes:
CAUSE: the old detail gate only looked at how much the colour texture was magnified on screen. The Pali detail patch stores 1.44 m texels, but much of its ground was filled in from 7-45 m sources (cres). So at 1-3 km the gate saw no magnification, added no detail, and left the smooth hazy band on the Pali right slope (2889-3148). After the fix that band shows canopy at full size and on the 390 px phone sheet; see crop_f003067_pali_right_slope_before_after.jpg.

(0) Every promoted region and stack I rendered loads with no errors and no 'det' error in any log: pali stack (ch2 frames, patch-edge test), halape/ch1, ch3, waimea, holei, midway, bigisland. Patch-edge test: I rendered a custom camera 1.3 km outside the pali_lookout east edge (dbg 6 plus the normal render). The gate goes from on to off over about 24 px at the edge. The fine-detail energy per row band stays level (18-20) and no line is visible, because the patch photo already carries the detail the gate removes.

(1) Stochastic tiling and the forest/grass split are in, at modest strength. Rock (1526, Hōlei), sand (7398), reef (Midway) and soil (Waimea) look the same or slightly better. After the final water fade, waimea, holei and midway were re-rendered: they differ from the earlier version by at most 0.033/255 on average. No vegetation on water or lava (dbg 7, Halapē, Hōlei).

(2) 'det' redeclaration: it came from a stale hand-copied hterrain.js in the staging tree scratchpad/closeup/www. The live file always had one declaration. Fixed by installing the live file; www2 and live are byte-identical.

(3) World-locked, no swimming:
- anchorShift (the 4 km anchor moved one step) leaves the frame identical: mean 0.16-0.24/255, and the 223 pixels over 4/255 are scattered, not in a line.
- Consecutive frames 2889 -> 2890: the fine detail moves with the 4-16 px band within 1 px in 38 of 39 boxes. The odd box holds the paper wall.
- 1 s apart (2889 -> 2919): the same holds in all 6 boxes that still correlate.

(4) Bigisland wides: no change, by design (identical pixels). At a 100 m+ footprint detail is rightly off. The softness comes from the 250 m MODIS colour and needs a finer colour bake, not a shader change. Separate finding: the cyan shallow-water rings around Maui Nui are stair-stepped (after_f004958_crop_maui_coast_ring.png). Likely cause, untested: the water edge glow is sized by fwidth of a bilinear coarse depth grid, whose slope jumps at every texel. The fix would be a smoother depth gradient in the water shader, which affects every water shot, so I did not touch it.

(5) Filtering, sharpening, haze: kept as they were (anisotropic colour and detail textures, colSharp 0.6 inside detFar, shared grade CAS 0.5 with no halo at the ridge/sky line, haze per shot only). crisp:0 still renders as a fallback.

NOT DONE:
- Pali lower third: limited by the photo (1.8-2.1 px per texel) and a 10 m interpolated height source.
- The pale veil under the wall: a bake issue, since cres marks it as fine photo.
- Steep faces keep the orthophoto stretch (Hōlei sea cliff, Pali flutes); a biplanar rock pass is the next step.

OTHER:
- No new sources or data were added, so SOURCES.md is unchanged. No baked data or media in git.
- Nothing committed or pushed. The chapter files were not touched (ch1-3 diffs in git are from the parallel builders).
- The LĀNAʻI label in the Hōlei test still is the fixed label of the toolkit_test.html region test (line 93), not a wrong region.
- Diff against the baseline: scratchpad/closeup/dev/hterrain.patch.

fixed: Contour stripes on Mauna Kea's summit cones (s065, frame 7349) are gone. They were a shading bug, not the data: they stayed with the patches, detail and shadows off, and the float DEM's own hillshade is clean. hterrain.js Hm() now reads float32 heights with a 4-tap bilinear of hTexF when crisp is on, instead of the half-float texture (2 m steps above 2,048 m). Promoted to live after a test-tree render. Pali changed by only 0.2/255 on average.

The cres mask is read at mip 3 or coarser (about 45 m), so the boundary between photo and procedural detail at Pali is a ramp, and small shadow pockets no longer turn into islands of crowns (dbg 6 at 3067).

From round 2, confirmed on the re-rendered stills: crisp Pali slopes and canopy (centre 0.75-1.1 px per colour texel in s026-s029), the real Kailua/Kawainui picture, the Kailua dive (3252), crisp Halapē lava and shore (1787), Kīlauea coast lava (1526) and the Mauna Kea cinder cones (7349).
New Q flag {"noPatch":1} (one line in shared.js) for before stills; with set.detAmt 0 it also turns off the detail texturing. Documented in API.md.
